references.text: The expression 'to know' (ידע) is used as a euphemism for sexual intercourse, just as it is used regarding the men of Sodom who wanted to 'know' Lot's guests.
A parallel event in Sodom where the men of the city surrounded the house and demanded to 'know' the guests, showing similar wickedness and violation of the laws of hospitality.
Shechem took Dinah, lay with her, and violated her; another account of sexual violence against a woman in the Old Testament.
Amnon raped his half-sister Tamar and then treated her with contempt, a parallel to the brutal treatment of the concubine.
The Levite's offer to give up his concubine to protect himself shows the context of how she was handed over to the mob.
The Levite's own account of the event to the tribes of Israel, where he tells that the men of Gibeah wanted to kill him and raped his concubine.
Hosea's symbolic act of taking a prostitute illustrates Israel's unfaithfulness and shows how sexual sin is used as an image of spiritual apostasy.
